claim.value: If responsibility ambiguity is absent, another candidate supported by evidence should be investigated.
claim.scope: A conditional redirection of the investigation, without identifying or asserting the existence of a particular alternative candidate.

provenance.rationale: The span supplies the absence condition and the evidence-qualified direction to investigate another candidate.

signal_basis.value: Checking whether attachment responsibility was unclear establishes the relevant absence condition. When ambiguity is absent, the proposed removal cannot be claimed, and investigation redirects to another evidenced candidate.
signal_basis.scope: The conditional absence branch of the investigation, rather than the prospective attachment-reduction signal.

provenance.rationale: The cited spans specify checking responsibility ambiguity and the investigative consequence if it is absent.
This supported procedural claim requires no unresolved empirical bridge.

rationale: An absent factor cannot undergo the proposed removal test. Redirecting investigation toward an evidence-supported candidate is therefore licensed as a procedural step within the stated bounds; it asserts neither an alternative cause nor the existence of a particular candidate.
uncertainty: Whether another evidenced candidate can actually be identified remains open and is not asserted by this claim.
